note:
ISO 2026-W26 runs from June 22 through June 28. Ceres is about 0.0° in ecliptic longitude from Aldebaran in Taurus.

**Naked eye:** No principal lunar phase is listed this week. Check the Moon's position each night and favor darker hours for low-contrast targets. Use Nekkar, Zubeneschamali as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -10.1; direct motion; 51.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mercury: Naked eye; magnitude 1.0; direct motion; 26.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -4.0; direct motion; 72.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.3; direct motion; 95.6% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 8.9; direct motion; 99.6% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -1.8; direct motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.8; direct motion; 99.7% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.5; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace the charted figure of Cir, then identify β Cir at its plotted position. Trace the charted figure of CrB, then identify Nusakan at its plotted position.

**Small telescope:** NGC 5823: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Spindle Galaxy: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Splinter Galaxy: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M5: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: Nekkar is a star in Boo of catalogue visual magnitude 3.49; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
The stored catalogue gives a visual magnitude of 3.49. This is a catalogue value, not a prediction of its brightness this week. Lower magnitudes mean brighter objects; sky brightness and altitude affect whether you can see the star.

Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 15h 01m and declination +40.4°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star rises and sets, reaching approximately 85° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Boo constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
